royal-hawaiian-hotel.name: Royal Hawaiian Hotel
royal-hawaiian-hotel.summary: A beachfront luxury hotel in Waikiki, Honolulu, one of the first hotels built there, nicknamed 'The Pink Palace of the Pacific' for its pink Spanish/Moorish-styled façade.

manapua.name: Manapua
manapua.summary: The Hawaiian adaptation of the Chinese steamed bun, especially char siu bao, whose name is a portmanteau roughly meaning "pork cake."

malassada.name: Malassada
malassada.summary: Portuguese fried doughnut from Madeira, coated in sugar and cinnamon, brought to Hawaii by Portuguese plantation workers.

pastel-food.name: Pastel
pastel-food.summary: The Spanish and Portuguese word for pastry, used across Latin America and Portugal for a range of sugary or savory filled dishes, varying by country.

cha-siu-bao.name: Char siu bao
cha-siu-bao.summary: A Cantonese steamed bun filled with barbecue-flavored pork, served as a type of dim sum during yum cha and sold in Chinese bakeries.

francisco-de-paula-mar-n.name: Francisco de Paula Marín
francisco-de-paula-mar-n.summary: Spaniard (1774–1837), also called Manini, who became a confidant of Hawaiian King Kamehameha I and introduced many agricultural products to the islands.

george-vancouver.name: George Vancouver
george-vancouver.summary: Royal Navy officer and explorer (1757–1798) who charted North America's northwestern Pacific coast; Vancouver Island and the city of Vancouver are named after him.

mission-grape.name: Mission grape
mission-grape.summary: A grape variety brought from Spain to the Americas by Catholic missionaries for making wine, still grown in Chile and Peru under other names.

adobo.name: Adobo
adobo.summary: A method of marinating food in vinegar, garlic, paprika, oregano and salt to preserve and flavor it, native to Iberia and later adapted independently in the Philippines using a similar vinegar-based technique.

volcano-school.name: The Volcano School
volcano-school.summary: A group of non-native Hawaiian artists in the 1880s-1890s who painted dramatic nighttime scenes of erupting volcanoes like Kilauea, blending European and American landscape traditions.

tapa-cloth.name: Tapa cloth
tapa-cloth.summary: A barkcloth made across the Pacific islands, especially Tonga, Samoa and Fiji; called kapa in Hawaii.

papeete-cathedral.name: Papeete Cathedral
papeete-cathedral.summary: A late 19th-century Catholic cathedral in Papeete, Tahiti, opened in 1875 as the oldest Catholic church on the island and one of its last colonial-era buildings.

james-cook.name: James Cook
james-cook.summary: A British Royal Navy officer, explorer and cartographer (1728-1779) who led three Pacific voyages, completed the first European circumnavigation of New Zealand's main islands, and led the first European visits to eastern Australia and Hawaii.

slack-key-guitar.name: Slack-key guitar
slack-key-guitar.summary: A Hawaiian fingerstyle guitar tradition using loosened, or 'slacked', string tunings to sound open chords, kept as family folk practice for generations.

mana-oceanic-cultures.name: Mana
mana-oceanic-cultures.summary: In Melanesian and Polynesian belief, a supernatural force thought to permeate the universe and be held by any person, object or place, seen as something to be cultivated rather than a source of power in itself.

moai.name: Moai
moai.summary: Monolithic stone figures carved by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island between 1250 and 1500, representing deified ancestors and set on platforms called ahu.

marquesas-islands.name: Marquesas Islands
marquesas-islands.summary: Volcanic island group in French Polynesia, settled around the 10th century AD by voyagers from West Polynesia and named after a 16th-century Spanish viceroy of Peru.

paul-gauguin.name: Paul Gauguin
paul-gauguin.summary: French Post-Impressionist and Symbolist painter (1848–1903) known for his experimental use of color and distinctive Synthetist style, though only moderately successful in his lifetime.

kingdom-of-tahiti.name: Kingdom of Tahiti
kingdom-of-tahiti.summary: A Polynesian monarchy founded by Pōmare I, unifying Tahiti and nearby islands with British missionary and European help, before becoming a French protectorate in 1842 and being annexed in 1880.

apostolic-vicariate.name: Apostolic vicariate
apostolic-vicariate.summary: A Catholic Church jurisdiction set up in mission territories before they have enough Catholics to become a full diocese, overseen directly by the Vatican.

kamehameha-i.name: Kamehameha I
kamehameha-i.summary: Conqueror and first ruler of the Kingdom of Hawaii, known as Kamehameha the Great, honored with a statue in the U.S. National Statuary Hall Collection.

kamehameha-ii.name: Liholiho (Kamehameha II)
kamehameha-ii.summary: Birth name of Kamehameha II, second king of Hawaii from 1819 to 1824, whose early power was limited by regent Kaʻahumanu; known for breaking traditional religious taboos.

sms-scharnhorst.name: SMS Scharnhorst
sms-scharnhorst.summary: The lead armored cruiser of the Imperial German Navy's East Asia Squadron, commissioned in 1907, which won the Battle of Coronel in 1914.

sms-gneisenau.name: SMS Gneisenau
sms-gneisenau.summary: An armored cruiser of the Imperial German Navy, launched in 1906, that served with the East Asia Squadron in the Pacific during World War I.

french-gunboat-z-l-e.name: Zélée
french-gunboat-z-l-e.summary: A French Navy gunboat used in Indochina and the Pacific, sunk while patrolling Tahiti during the German bombardment of Papeete on 22 September 1914.

papeete.name: Papeete
papeete.summary: The capital of French Polynesia, on the island of Tahiti, and the territory's main center of government, commerce and tourism; its name means 'water from a basket.'

lili-uokalani.name: Liliʻuokalani
lili-uokalani.summary: Last sovereign monarch of the Hawaiian Kingdom, reigning 1891–1893 until overthrown in a coup; composed the song "Aloha ʻOe" and wrote her autobiography while imprisoned.

john-l-stevens.name: John L. Stevens
john-l-stevens.summary: American politician who served as US Minister to the Hawaiian Kingdom and conspired with the Committee of Safety to overthrow Queen Liliuokalani in 1893; also a journalist and founder of Maine's Republican Party.

committee-of-safety-hawaii.name: Committee of Safety
committee-of-safety-hawaii.summary: A 13-member group of American and Hawaiian-American residents that planned and carried out the 1893 overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom, aiming for annexation by the United States.

p-mare-ii.name: Pōmare II
p-mare-ii.summary: Second king of Tahiti, ruling from 1791 to 1821 after being installed by his father Pōmare I, initially under regency until 1803.

p-mare-iv.name: Pōmare IV
p-mare-iv.summary: Queen of Tahiti from 1827 to 1877 and the fourth monarch of the Kingdom of Tahiti, also known as ʻAimata.

teriitaria-ii.name: Teriitaria II
teriitaria-ii.summary: Queen consort of Tahiti through her marriage to Pōmare II and later ruler of Huahine and Maiao, who led forces that repelled a French invasion at the Battle of Maeva in 1846.

huahine.name: Huahine
huahine.summary: An island in French Polynesia's Society Islands, part of the Leeward Islands group, with a population of about 6,263 as of 2022.

jarnac-convention.name: Jarnac Convention
jarnac-convention.summary: An 1847 agreement between France and Britain ending tension after the Franco-Tahitian War by guaranteeing independence for Polynesia's Leeward Islands; abolished by mutual consent in 1887.

maxime-destremau.name: Maxime Destremau
maxime-destremau.summary: French naval lieutenant who served in World War I and was notable for his role during the Bombardment of Papeete.

uss-boston-1884.name: USS Boston
uss-boston-1884.summary: A US Navy protected cruiser commissioned in the 1880s, among the first steel warships of the 'New Navy,' whose landed marines helped depose Hawaii's Queen Lili'uokalani in 1893.

battle-of-coronel.name: Battle of Coronel
battle-of-coronel.summary: A First World War naval battle on 1 November 1914 off Chile in which a German squadron under Maximilian von Spee defeated a British force, a shock that led Britain to send ships that later destroyed the German fleet.

battle-of-the-falkland-islands.name: Battle of the Falkland Islands
battle-of-the-falkland-islands.summary: A First World War naval battle on 8 December 1914 off the Falkland Islands, where a British squadron hunted down and destroyed most of the German cruiser squadron that had earlier won at Coronel.

robert-henry-codrington.name: Robert Henry Codrington
robert-henry-codrington.summary: Robert Henry Codrington: English Anglican missionary and anthropologist (1830-1922) who made the first study of Melanesian society and popularized the concept of mana in the West.

orenda.name: Orenda
orenda.summary: A term coined in 1902 for a theorized Iroquoian belief in an invisible spiritual force pervading people and nature, compared by scholars to mana.

haudenosaunee.name: Haudenosaunee
haudenosaunee.summary: A confederacy of Iroquoian-speaking peoples in northeast North America, originally five (later six) nations united under the Great Law of Peace, called the Iroquois by Europeans.

marae.name: Marae
marae.summary: A communal or sacred cleared ground used for religious and social purposes in Polynesian societies, still vital in some cultures today though abandoned in others after Christianity arrived.

william-colenso.name: William Colenso
william-colenso.summary: Cornish Christian missionary to New Zealand (1811–1899), also a printer, botanist, explorer and politician; attended the 1840 signing of the Treaty of Waitangi.

kioea.name: Kioea
kioea.summary: An extinct species of Hawaiian honeyeater endemic to the islands of Hawaii, which died out around the mid-19th century.

hawaiian-kingdom.name: Hawaiian Kingdom
hawaiian-kingdom.summary: An archipelagic Pacific state from 1795 to 1893, unified by Kamehameha I, which gained international recognition before being overthrown in an 1893 coup backed by the US military.

queen-emma-of-hawaii.name: Queen Emma of Hawaii
queen-emma-of-hawaii.summary: Queen of Hawaii as wife of King Kamehameha IV from 1856 to 1863, later known as a humanitarian who established a hospital and is venerated in the Episcopal Church.

kamehameha-iv.name: Kamehameha IV
kamehameha-iv.summary: Fourth king of Hawaii, born Alexander Liholiho, who reigned from 1855 to 1863.

republic-of-hawaii.name: Republic of Hawaii
republic-of-hawaii.summary: A one-party state governing Hawaii from 1894, after the overthrow of Queen Liliʻuokalani, until it was annexed by the United States in 1898.

p-mare-v.name: Pōmare V
p-mare-v.summary: The last monarch of Tahiti, son of Queen Pōmare IV, who reigned from 1877 until his forced abdication in 1880.

chesse.name: Henri Isidore Chessé
chesse.summary: French colonial governor of Tahiti from 1880 to 1881.

george-tupou-i.name: Tāufaʻāhau
george-tupou-i.summary: Original name of George Tupou I, the first king of modern Tonga, who expanded his rule from a disputed territory in Ha'apai to unite the islands.

shirley-waldemar-baker.name: Shirley Waldemar Baker
shirley-waldemar-baker.summary: Methodist missionary (1836–1903) in Tonga who founded the Free Church of Tonga and served as prime minister under King George Tupou I.

kamehameha-iii.name: Kamehameha III
kamehameha-iii.summary: Third king of Hawaii (1825–1854), born Kauikeaouli, the monarchy's longest-reigning ruler, who introduced Hawaii's first constitutions in 1840 and 1852.

great-m-hele.name: Great Māhele
great-m-hele.summary: A Hawaiian land redistribution proposed by King Kamehameha III, one of the most important episodes in Hawaiian history, meant to secure land title for Indigenous Hawaiians but which ended up separating many from their land.

john-c-calhoun.name: John C. Calhoun
john-c-calhoun.summary: American statesman (1782–1850), seventh US vice president, who shifted from nationalism to championing states' rights and slavery, influencing the South's later secession.

john-tyler.name: John Tyler
john-tyler.summary: Tenth U.S. president (1841–1845), a Virginia states'-rights advocate who became estranged from both major parties after succeeding William Henry Harrison.

abel-aubert-du-petit-thouars.name: Abel Aubert du Petit-Thouars
abel-aubert-du-petit-thouars.summary: French naval officer (1793–1864) who played a leading role in establishing French Polynesia.

franco-tahitian-war.name: Franco-Tahitian War
franco-tahitian-war.summary: Conflict from 1844 to 1847 between the Kingdom of France and the Kingdom of Tahiti and its allies, sparked by the expulsion of French Catholic missionaries and ending in French control.

kal-kaua.name: Kalākaua
kal-kaua.summary: Last king of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi, reigning from 1874 to 1891, nicknamed the 'Merrie Monarch' for reviving the hula, and known for a world tour and lavish spending.

reciprocity-treaty-of-1875.name: Reciprocity Treaty of 1875
reciprocity-treaty-of-1875.summary: An 1875 free trade agreement giving Hawaiian sugar and other products duty-free access to U.S. markets in exchange for Hawaii's promise not to cede land to other foreign powers.

ford-island.name: Ford Island
ford-island.summary: An islet in Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, once the site of a Hawaiian fertility ritual and later a sugarcane plantation, that became a U.S. Navy base and was central to the 1941 attack on Pearl Harbor.

kapi-olani.name: Kapiʻolani
kapi-olani.summary: Queen of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi as consort of King Kalākaua, who reigned 1874 to 1891; she founded institutions caring for Native Hawaiian mothers, newborns, and the daughters of leprosy patients.

queen-victoria.name: Queen Victoria
queen-victoria.summary: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1837 to 1901, whose 63-year reign, longer than any predecessor's, saw great expansion of the British Empire; she was proclaimed Empress of India in 1876.

charles-barff-missionary.name: Charles Barff
charles-barff-missionary.summary: English missionary (1791-1866) who helped spread Christianity and reshape culture and religion across Polynesia in the 19th century.

george-seymour-royal-navy-officer.name: George Seymour
george-seymour-royal-navy-officer.summary: Royal Navy admiral who fought in the Napoleonic Wars and War of 1812, and as Commander-in-Chief Pacific Station tactfully defused the 1844 dispute with France over Tahiti.

leeward-islands-society-islands.name: Leeward Islands
leeward-islands-society-islands.summary: The western islands of French Polynesia's Society Islands, including Huahine and Raiatea, covering about 404 square kilometers with over 36,000 people.

ra-i-tea.name: Ra'iātea
ra-i-tea.summary: The second-largest of the Society Islands in French Polynesia, regarded as the ancient centre of eastern Polynesia and likely starting point of migrations to Hawaii and other Pacific islands.

ka-ahumanu.name: Kaʻahumanu
ka-ahumanu.summary: Queen consort and regent (Kuhina Nui) of the Hawaiian Kingdom, the most politically powerful wife of King Kamehameha I.

ke-p-olani.name: Keōpūolani
ke-p-olani.summary: A queen consort of Hawaiʻi (1778–1823) and the highest-ranking wife of King Kamehameha I.

ali-i.name: Aliʻi
ali-i.summary: Traditional hereditary nobility of the Hawaiian islands, spanning several ranks of chiefs that could be held by men or women.

k-ne.name: Kāne
k-ne.summary: The highest of the three major Hawaiian deities, worshipped as the god of procreation, creator of life, and ancestor of chiefs and commoners, associated with dawn, sun and sky.

k.name: Kū
k.summary: One of the four great gods of Hawaiian religion, worshiped under many names including Kūkāʻilimoku, whose rites uniquely included human sacrifice.

lono.name: Lono
lono.summary: A Hawaiian god of fertility, agriculture, rain, music and peace, honored during the annual Makahiki festival.

kanaloa.name: Kanaloa
kanaloa.summary: A Hawaiian god symbolized by the squid or octopus, associated with the ocean and seamanship, and traditionally paired with the god Kāne.

kahuna.name: Kahuna
kahuna.summary: Hawaiian word for an expert in any field, historically used for priests, doctors, ministers and sorcerers.

london-missionary-society.name: London Missionary Society
london-missionary-society.summary: An interdenominational evangelical missionary society founded in England in 1795 that sent missionaries to places including Tahiti, China and Africa.

george-pritchard-missionary.name: George Pritchard
george-pritchard-missionary.summary: British missionary who worked in the Society Islands from 1824 and became British consul at Tahiti, advising Queen Pōmare IV until France annexed the islands in 1843.

fa-a-s-moa.name: Faʻa Sāmoa
fa-a-s-moa.summary: The traditional, customary way of life in Samoan culture.

aumakua.name: ʻAumakua
aumakua.summary: In Hawaiian belief, a personal or family guardian spirit descended from a deified ancestor, often taking the form of an animal such as a shark or owl.

mililani-trask.name: Mililani Trask
mililani-trask.summary: Leader of the Hawaiian sovereignty movement, attorney and political speaker who founded Na Koa Ikaika o Ka Lāhui Hawaiʻi and helped author the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.

native-hawaiians.name: Kanaka Maoli
native-hawaiians.summary: Indigenous Polynesian people of the Hawaiian Islands, settled at least 800 years ago, who developed a distinct culture and formed the Hawaiian Kingdom in 1795 under Kamehameha the Great.

lauhala.name: Lauhala
lauhala.summary: The leaves of the hala tree (Pandanus tectorius); 'lau' means leaf in Hawaiian, and the leaves were traditionally used for weaving.

hawai-i-pono.name: Hawaiʻi Ponoʻī
hawai-i-pono.summary: The anthem of the U.S. state of Hawaii, formerly the national anthem of the independent Hawaiian Kingdom and Republic of Hawaii, kept in use since annexation in 1898.

henri-berger.name: Henri Berger
henri-berger.summary: Prussian-born bandmaster (1844 to 1929) who served the Kingdom of Hawaii from 1872 to 1915 and composed the music for its national anthem.

he-mele-l-hui-hawai-i.name: He Mele Lāhui Hawaiʻi
he-mele-l-hui-hawai-i.summary: A song composed by Liliʻuokalani in 1866 at King Kamehameha V's request to give Hawaii a national anthem in place of the British anthem; it served as the anthem for about a decade.

lahaina-hawaii.name: Lahaina
lahaina-hawaii.summary: A coastal town on Maui, Hawaii, once a major whaling port, largely destroyed by wildfires in 2023.

jules-dumont-d-urville.name: Jules Dumont d'Urville
jules-dumont-d-urville.summary: French explorer and naval officer, 1790 to 1842, who explored the Pacific, Australia, New Zealand and Antarctica, giving his name to several places as a botanist and cartographer.

soci-t-de-g-ographie.name: Société de Géographie
soci-t-de-g-ographie.summary: The world's oldest geographical society, founded in Paris in 1821, which has published a journal since 1822 and hosted major geographic lectures and decisions.

albert-kamehameha.name: Albert Kamehameha
albert-kamehameha.summary: Only son of King Kamehameha IV and Queen Emma of Hawaii, and Crown Prince of the Kingdom of Hawaii, who died in 1862 at age four; godson of Queen Victoria.
